The public library bills overdue fees once a month from the circulation exports of its branches, in /app/data. Write a Python script at /app/bin/fees.py that turns the exports and the lending files into the fee statements by the rules in /app/docs (start with /app/docs/overview.md) and writes the statements file described in /app/docs/output.md. It is run as `python3 /app/bin/fees.py INPUT_DIR OUTPUT_FILE`. Run it on /app/data and save the result as /app/out/statements.json.

From /app, `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` runs the script on a few small inputs, and `python tools/check_fees.py` compares /app/out/statements.json with the approved statements for the current period. The script will also be run on the exports and lending files of other periods, with other branches, patrons and calendars, so it must follow the documented rules rather than what the current files happen to contain. Use only the Python standard library. Do not change anything under /app/data, /app/docs, /app/tests or /app/tools.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

1 	# Overdue fee statements: overview
2 	
3 	The library lends books, DVDs, magazines, laptops and kits from its
4 	branches. Once a month the fee run reads the circulation exports of every
5 	branch together with the lending policy, and writes one fee statement per
6 	patron with overdue loans and a summary per branch. This note says what goes
7 	in, what comes out and in which order the work is done. The rules for each
8 	step live in their own notes:
9 	
10	| Note | Covers |
11	|---|---|
12	| `lending.md` | the lending files: policy, branches, calendar, patrons, waivers |
13	| `exports.md` | the circulation export files and their events, local times, voids |
14	| `loans.md` | how events become loans: due dates, renewals, returns, the period |
15	| `fees.md` | overdue days, grace, the fee of a loan, waivers, the statement cap |
16	| `output.md` | the statements file |
17	| `changelog.md` | what changed between versions of these rules |
18

<path>docs/loans.md</path>
<content>
1 	# Loans
2 	
3 	## 1. Checkouts
4 	
5 	1.1 A loan starts with a checkout event that is not cancelled. The loan id
6 	is the `loan` of the checkout, the patron is its `patron`, the item type its
7 	`item_type`, the checkout branch its `branch`, and the checkout date its local
8 	date. Two checkouts that count never share a loan id.
9 	
10	1.2 A checkout dated after `period_end` is not part of the run, and neither
11	are the events of its loan.
12	
13	1.3 A renewal or a return whose loan id has no checkout that counts belongs
14	to no loan and changes nothing.
15	
16	## 2. The due date
17	
18	2.1 The due date of a loan is its checkout date plus `loan_days` of the item
19	type.
20	
21	2.2 When the checkout branch is closed on that day (`lending.md` 3.5), the
22	due date moves to the next day on which the checkout branch is open.
23	
24	## 3. Renewals and returns
25	
26	The renewals and returns of a loan are taken in the order of their local
27	times. Two events of one loan never share a local time.
28	
29	3.1 A renewal counts only when all of these hold:
30	
31	- (a) its local date is on or before the due date of the loan at that moment;
32	- (b) the loan has fewer counted renewals than `renewals` of the item type;
33	- (c) its local date is on or before `period_end`.
34	
35	A renewal that does not count changes nothing; in particular it does not use
36	up one of the renewals of (b).
37	
38	3.2 A counted renewal sets the due date to its local date plus `loan_days`,
39	moved to the next open day of the checkout branch as in 2.2.
40	
41	3.3 The first return ends the loan. Events of the loan after it change
42	nothing.
43	
44	## 4. The return date
45	
46	4.1 The return date of a loan is the local date of its return event.
47	
48	4.2 A return with `via` `dropbox` came through the book drop, which is
49	emptied and checked in at the start of a working day. Its return date is the
50	day before the local date of the return event.
51	
52	## 5. The period
53	
54	5.1 The fee run is made as of `period_end`. A loan whose return date is
55	after `period_end` is still out at the end of the period, and its return is
56	not used by this run. A book-drop return checked in after `period_end` can
57	still have a return date inside the period (4.2).
58	
59	5.2 The loans of the run are the loans of section 1 that were not returned
60	before `period_start`: a loan with a return date before `period_start` is
61	not part of the run.
</content>

<path>docs/fees.md</path>
<content>
1 	# Fees
2 	
3 	All amounts are whole cents. `policy.ini` values are those of the item type
4 	of the loan and of the patron's category named in each rule.
5 	
6 	## 1. Overdue days
7 	
8 	1.1 The overdue days of a loan are the days after its due date, up to and
9 	including its end day, on which the checkout branch is open (`lending.md`
10	3.5). The end day is the return date, or `period_end` for a loan still out at
11	the end of the period (`loans.md` 5.1). Days on which the checkout branch is
12	closed are never overdue days, whatever branch the item is returned to.
13	
14	1.2 Grace allowance, by `grace_days` of the item type:
15	
16	- A loan with no more overdue days than `grace_days` is charged for none of them.
17	- A loan with more overdue days than `grace_days` is charged for every one of its overdue days, the first ones included.
18	
19	1.3 The charged days of a loan are the overdue days it is charged for.
20	
21	## 2. The assessed fee of a loan
22	
23	2.1 The base fee is the charged days times `daily`.
24	
25	2.2 When the item type is listed in `exempt` of the patron's category on the
26	checkout date, the base fee is 0.
27	
28	2.3 The base fee is cut to `loan_cap` when it is higher.
29	
30	2.4 The discount of the patron's category on the checkout date is taken off
31	the result of 2.3: the assessed fee is that amount times (100 minus
32	`discount`) divided by 100, rounded to a whole cent, with half a cent
33	rounded up. With a discount of 50, 125 cents give 63.
34	
35	## 3. Waivers
36	
37	3.1 A waiver applies to a loan of a statement when it is active, its patron
38	is the patron of the loan (`lending.md` 5), and its `loan` is the loan id or
39	`*`.
40	
41	3.2 When a waiver that applies is `full`, the waived amount is the assessed
42	fee. Otherwise the waived amount is the sum of the amounts of the waivers that
43	apply, but never more than the assessed fee. A `*` waiver with an amount
44	applies that amount to each loan of the statement.
45	
46	3.3 The net fee of a loan is its assessed fee minus its waived amount.
47	
48	## 4. The statement cap
49	
50	4.1 The statement cap is `statement_cap` of the patron's category on
51	`period_end`. With `none` there is no cap.
52	
53	4.2 When the net fees of the loans of a statement add up to more than the
54	cap, the excess is capped. It is taken from the loans in order of due date,
55	latest first, and for loans with the same due date, from the loan id that
56	sorts last as text first. Each loan gives up as much of its net fee as the
57	excess still needs, and no more than its net fee.
58	
59	4.3 The billed fee of a loan is its net fee minus what it gave up to the cap.
60	
61	## 5. Which loans are on a statement
62	
63	5.1 A statement lists every loan of the patron that is part of the run
64	(`loans.md` 5.2) and has at least one overdue day, including loans charged
65	nothing because of grace, an exemption or a waiver.
66	
67	5.2 A patron with no such loan gets no statement.
</content>

51	(`loans.md` 2 and 3), written `YYYY-MM-DD`.
52	
53	3.3 `returned` is the return date when it is on or before `period_end`, and
54	`null` for a loan still out at the end of the period.
55	
56	3.4 `overdue_days` and `charged_days` follow `fees.md` 1. `assessed` is the
57	assessed fee (`fees.md` 2), `waived` the waived amount (`fees.md` 3), `capped`
58	what the loan gave up to the statement cap (`fees.md` 4) and `billed` the
59	billed fee. All amounts are whole cents.
60	
61	## 4. The branch summary
62	
63	4.1 `branches` has one entry per branch of `branches.csv`, in the order of
64	that file, branches without loans on any statement included.
65	
66	4.2 `loans` counts the statement loans whose checkout branch is the branch.
67	`charged_days`, `assessed`, `waived`, `capped` and `billed` are the sums of
68	the same fields over those loans.
69	
70	## 5. Checking
71	
72	From `/app`:
73	
74	- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` runs the program on a few small
75	  inputs and compares each result with the reviewed one next to it.
76	- `python tools/check_fees.py` runs the program on `/app/data` and on a copy
77	  of it in another directory, compares `/app/out/statements.json` with the
78	  approved statements of the current period and names the first statements
79	  that differ. The approved statements are stored as salted digests, so the
80	  check says whether a statement is right, never what it should hold.

<path>docs/exports.md</path>
<content>
1 	# Circulation exports
2 	
3 	## 1. Files
4 	
5 	1.1 `exports/` holds the files that the circulation system of each branch
6 	exports. Only files whose names end in `.csv` or `.jsonl` are exports. Other
7 	files are not: the manifest, and files that a branch is still writing, which
8 	end in `.part` until they are complete.
9 	
10	1.2 A file is UTF-8 text with LF line ends. It can begin with a byte order
11	mark.
12	
13	1.3 Exports overlap. A branch exports a span of days, and its next file can
14	start up to two days before the previous one ended; a resend file repeats
15	events that a branch sent again. An event is identified by its `event` id: it
16	appears in any number of files, always with the same fields, and it counts
17	once.
18	
19	## 2. CSV exports
20	
21	2.1 The first line names the columns. The order of the columns differs
22	between files, and some files carry more columns than section 4 names; a
23	program finds the columns by name and ignores the others. A cell with nothing
24	to say is empty.
25	
26	2.2 Column `time` is the local time of the event at the library, written
27	`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` (section 5).
28	
29	## 3. JSON Lines exports
30	
31	3.1 Each line is one JSON object with the fields of section 4, except that
32	`at` takes the place of `time`. Fields with nothing to say are left out.
33	
34	3.2 `at` is the instant of the event, written in ISO 8601 with seconds and
35	either `Z` (UTC) or an offset from UTC: `2027-02-03T04:12:00Z`,
36	`2027-02-02T22:12:00-06:00`. Both forms name an instant; section 5 turns it
37	into a local time.
38	
39	## 4. Fields of an event
40	
41	| Field | Holds |
42	|---|---|
43	| `event` | the event id |
44	| `type` | `checkout`, `renew`, `return` or `void`, in any case |
45	| `loan` | the loan id (checkout, renew, return) |
46	| `patron` | the patron number (checkout), in any of the forms of `lending.md` 5 |
47	| `item` | the item barcode (checkout, return) |
48	| `item_type` | the item type (checkout), in any case |
49	| `branch` | the id of the branch where the event happened |
50	| `via` | `desk`, `self`, `online` or `dropbox` |
51	| `target` | the event id that a void cancels (void only) |
52	
53	## 5. Local time
54	
55	5.1 Every rule of these notes works on local dates of the library. The local
56	time of a CSV event is its `time`. The local time of a JSON Lines event is
57	its instant shifted by the offset of `policy.ini` `[clock]` in force at that
58	instant (`lending.md` 1.3).
59	
60	5.2 The local date of an event is the date of its local time.
61	
62	## 6. Voids
63	
64	6.1 A `void` event cancels the event named by its `target`. A cancelled event
65	counts nowhere: a cancelled checkout starts no loan, a cancelled renewal or
66	return does not happen.
67	
68	6.2 A void is not an event of any loan, and voids are never cancelled.
</content>

1 	# Changelog of the fee rules
2 	
3 	## 4.0 (2026-09)
4 	
5 	- A loan past its grace allowance is charged for every overdue day, the
6 	  first ones included (`fees.md` 1.2). Up to 3.x the grace days were
7 	  deducted from the charged days.
8 	- Exemptions and discounts follow the patron's category on the checkout
9 	  date (`fees.md` 2.2 and 2.4); the statement cap follows the category on
10	  `period_end` (`fees.md` 4.1). 3.x used the category on `period_end` for
11	  all three.
12	- `*` waivers cover every loan of a patron's statement (`lending.md` 6).
13	
14	## 3.1 (2026-03)
15	
16	- The discount is rounded half up to a whole cent (`fees.md` 2.4). 3.0
17	  rounded half to even, so 62.5 cents became 62.
18	- The loan cap is applied before the discount (`fees.md` 2.3 and 2.4).
19	
20	## 3.0 (2025-11)
21	
22	- Only days on which the checkout branch is open are overdue days
23	  (`fees.md` 1.1). Up to 2.x every calendar day after the due date counted.
24	- A book-drop return is dated the day before it is checked in (`loans.md`
25	  4.2).
26	- `calendar.csv` takes ranges of days and `open` rows; a row for one branch
27	  takes precedence over a `*` row for the same day (`lending.md` 3.5).
28	
29	## 2.0 (2025-04)
30	
31	- JSON Lines exports write instants in UTC or with an offset; local dates
32	  come from the `[clock]` section of `policy.ini`, which lists the changes of
33	  the library's offset (`exports.md` 5).
34	- The excess over the statement cap is taken from the loans due last
35	  (`fees.md` 4.2), so the oldest charges stay on the bill.
36	- Renewals made after the due date, or beyond the renewal limit, do not
37	  count (`loans.md` 3.1).
</content>

## 1. policy.ini

1.1 `policy.ini` is an INI file: sections in square brackets, one
`key = value` per line, and comment lines that start with `#`. Values have no
quotes. Amounts of money are written in currency units with two decimals
(`0.25`) and stand for whole cents (25).

1.2 Section `[statement]`: `library` (the library's name), `period_start` and
`period_end` (dates `YYYY-MM-DD`, both included in the period).

1.3 Section `[clock]`: the library's offset from UTC.

- `offset` is the offset in force before the first change, written `-06:00`.
- `changes` lists the changes, separated by `;`, in time order. Each change
  is an instant in UTC written `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ`, a space and the offset in
  force from that instant on. `changes` can be empty.

1.4 One section `[item:TYPE]` per item type (`[item:book]`, `[item:dvd]`):

- `loan_days`: days from a checkout or a counted renewal to the due date
  (`loans.md` 2 and 3);
- `renewals`: the most renewals of one loan that count (`loans.md` 3.1);
- `grace_days`: the grace allowance (`fees.md` 1.2);
- `daily`: the fee per charged day;
- `loan_cap`: the most that one loan of this type is assessed before a
  discount (`fees.md` 2.3).

1.5 One section `[category:NAME]` per patron category:

- `statement_cap`: the most that one statement of a patron of this category
  bills (`fees.md` 4), or `none` for no cap;
- `discount`: a whole percentage taken off the fee of each loan (`fees.md`
  2.4), 0 for none;
- `exempt`: item types, separated by commas, whose loans this category is
  never charged for (`fees.md` 2.2); it can be empty.

Item types and category names are compared without regard to case.

## 2. branches.csv

2.1 Columns `branch`, `name`, `open_days`. `open_days` lists the weekdays on
which the branch opens, as three-letter English names separated by spaces
(`Tue Wed Thu Fri Sat`).

2.2 The order of the rows is the order of the branch summary (`output.md`
4.1).

## 3. calendar.csv

3.1 Columns `date`, `branch`, `status`, `note`. The note carries nothing for
the fee run.

3.2 `date` is one day (`2027-02-15`) or a range of days `FIRST..LAST`
